title: Self Assessment late filing and payment penalties overview
summary: If you miss Self Assessment filing or payment deadlines you may have to pay penalties and interest. Penalty amounts and timing depend on how late you are and HMRC rules for the period. Check GOV.UK Self Assessment penalties guidance for current details rather than relying on memory.

title: Records you should keep if self-employed
summary: If you are self-employed you must keep records of business income and expenses. Keep records for at least 5 years after the 31 January submission deadline of the relevant tax year. Digital record-keeping becomes especially important under Making Tax Digital.

title: Cryptoassets and tax overview
summary: HMRC treats cryptoassets as potentially taxable. Depending on your activity you may need to consider Capital Gains Tax and/or Income Tax. Keep detailed records of transactions. Check GOV.UK cryptoassets tax guidance for how your situation may be treated.

title: PAYE employment plus additional income
summary: Being taxed under PAYE does not automatically mean you have no Self Assessment obligations. Additional untaxed income, self-employment, property income or other criteria can still mean you need to file a return. Check GOV.UK ‘who must send a tax return’.

title: Trading allowance overview
summary: There is a trading allowance that can apply to certain trading or casual income up to a set amount, subject to conditions. Confirm the current allowance figure and eligibility on GOV.UK before relying on it.

title: Property allowance overview
summary: A property allowance may apply to certain property income up to a set amount, subject to conditions and interactions with other reliefs. Confirm current figures and eligibility on GOV.UK.

title: Self Assessment paper filing deadline
summary: If you file a paper Self Assessment return, the usual deadline is 31 October following the end of the tax year. Online filing is normally due by 31 January. Confirm current deadlines on GOV.UK.

title: Reporting Capital Gains Tax
summary: Depending on the asset and timing, Capital Gains Tax may be reported through Self Assessment and/or a dedicated reporting service (for example for UK property in some cases). Check GOV.UK for the correct reporting route and deadlines.
